utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Maybe it's advisable that we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. On the 13th of April, 2006, the Prosecution filed a motion for admission of statements of witnesses MM-16 and MM-18 pursuant to Rule 89(F). The Prosecution seeks the admission into evidence of, one, the statement of MM-016 with Annexes 1 to 3 and 5; and, two, the statement of MM-018 with Annex 2. In its response of 27 April 2006, the Defence did not object to the admission of those statements and annexes. The Trial Chamber notes that Rule 89(C) and (F) that it is well established in the jurisprudence that witness statements may be admitted into evidence under Rule 89(F) provided certain conditions are met. The determination of the interests of justice under Rule 89(F) is to be made in relation to each individual witness in light not only of the surrounding circumstances but also the evidence to be given by the witness. The Trial Chamber notes that the witnesses will be present in court to attest to the accuracy of their respective statements and annexes and for questioning by the Defence and the Trial Chamber. The Trial Chamber therefore finds that it is in the interests of justice to admit the statements with annexes into evidence and requests the registrar to assign exhibit numbers out of court. That's the end of the decision. Then we also had the Prosecution motion for admission of additional written statements of Witness MM-083. On the 3rd of May, the Prosecutor filed a confidential motion for admission of additional written statement pursuant to Rule 92 bis and for -- I'm not quite sure whether we shouldn't go into private session as this one says "protective measures." Maybe we should.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We will are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may call the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if we could bring Mr. Kerkkanen back in, please. Just while we're waiting, just so as a reminder to myself that there are one or two housekeeping matters that we have after the witness, just to alert the Court. Hopefully I'll remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Whiting. You're obviously not relying on the Court to remind you. It forgets much worse than counsel does.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't ask that of the Court, Your Honour. It was a way of making myself remember. I thought if I said it out loud and it was on the transcript it would help me remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, first of all let me remind you that you are bound by the statement you made at the beginning to tell the truth, the whole truth and nothing else but the truth. Having said that, let me just express the Court's regret that you have been kept here waiting the whole of yesterday perhaps not knowing what's happening. Due to circumstances beyond the control of all of us in court, we are not able to sit today. We are only able to continue with your testimony today. We hope you can bear with us. Thank you very much. Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, sir. We shall continue the cross-examination. I would kindly ask you to turn to the second part of the annex in B/C/S. This is 27, and the title is MUP SAO Krajina, Crimes Committed in 1991. And this page starts with the footnote 132, for easier identification of the page. At the very beginning of this page, sir, you say this: "Martic and Captain Dragan gave instructions to the War Staffs of the municipalities of Dvor, Glina, and Kostajnica in the area of Banja and Kordun and they participated in a meeting held on 23rd July in the War Staff of the municipality of Dvor in Samarica." With this regard, I would kindly ask you to point to the document which provided the basis for you to say that Martic, the accused in this case, provided War Staffs with instructions. If I may be of any assistance, at the end of this page you are saying in the report on the operation that took place on the 26th of June, 1991, it says that the plan for the operation came from Captain Dragan and the War Staff in Glina. This is just for clarification, to clarify my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down, Mr. Milovancevic. I can hear the interpreter rattling away trying to keep pace with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreter. I will bear that in mind, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: At the very end of that page, you are saying the report on the operation that took place on the 26th of July says that the plan for the operation came from Captain Dragan, and at the beginning you are saying Martic and Captain Dragan provided instructions. So could you please point to the document where you found that Martic provided instructions.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not explicitly said in this document that he provided instructions, and as you referred, the document Exhibit number 2039 states that the plan was received from Captain Dragan and that Glina War Staff for this operation. However, taking into account Martic's position and his presence in this meeting on the 23rd of July, my interpretation is that he was there in his capacity as minister of the interior. Therefore, there must be some meaning in his presence at this particular time just prior to this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, was your task to interpret military or any other instructions or to locate and identify documents? What was your task?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My task was to locate and identify relevant documents pertaining to the SAO Krajina MUP and the RSK MUP and to write a report on the basis of these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see on the ELMO or on the screen document 25? That is Prosecutor's document 25 from the 65 ter list. Can we see that on the screen, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is not the document that I asked for. Could you please bear with me just a moment. I would like to check that in the footnote. When I asked for 2025 document to be shown on the screen, I referred to the footnote 133 that mentions document 2025, and the report is entitled report for July -- report for 23rd July in the War Staff of Samarica municipality and signed by the chief of the War Staff. I have this document in B/C/S. It's an entirely different document, the one that I have just mentioned. So it is not the document that is on the screen but the document that is referred to in footnote 133. So could I please have the document from -- referred to in 133, and its number is 2025. In order to save time, I don't have to insist on the document. We'll see whether it will be necessary. I'm going to show the witness the following and tell him the following:

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the document that you mention in footnote 133, Mr. Kerkkanen, you are -- the document in its first paragraph speaks about no changes that have taken place --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may just be of assistance. First of all, I think the initial confusion was because it was interpreted as 25 rather than 2025, but it appears that -- that 2025, there's nothing in e-court under that 65 ter number, but the document that I believe counsel is looking for is under 1219, 65 ter number 1219. So if that's of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Let's have a look at document 1219 and see whether it will be the document that counsel wants to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank my learned friend for assistance with this matter. This is the document that I had in mind, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the first paragraph of this document, Mr. Kerkkanen, it says as follows: There were no changes on the front line, which was 18 kilometres long. From the Dvor barricade to the rail station in Volinja. Further on it says in the last paragraph: After the Defence minister and commanders addressed all present. Is it based, on this document, that you concluded that Mr. Martic, as you say in the first paragraph, provided instructions?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of the documents that saw Mr. Martic being present on the 23rd of July, 1991. In this meeting, there's also Exhibit number 2013, which states Martic was sitting there on the 23rd of July, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: It is precisely because of your answer and the contents of the document my question was as follows: You make a conclusion based on the fact that Mr. Martic was there, that he himself provided instructions to the War Staffs. Am I right in saying that and in thinking that?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: With regard to this situation in Dvor, these documents speak about the month of July 1991. One of the documents that I would like to be shown on the screen is Prosecutor's document 2409. One of the documents is the decision of the Municipal Assembly of Glina dated 31st March 1991, on separating the police station in Glina from the strength of the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Croatia and on joining that police station to the SAO Krajina SUP. Do you remember any such document, Mr. Kerkkanen? You can already see the document on the screen. Can you scroll up a bit so that the witness can see the whole content of the decision? According to this document, should the police station in Glina be in the hands of the Serb authorities as of the 31st of March, 1991? Would you agree with that, Mr. Kerkkanen?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the decision that this document states, but it doesn't mean that the police station physically was in the hands of the SAO Krajina authorities at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is it factually indisputable that on the 26th of July and 27th of July, i.e., towards the end of July 1991, there were skirmishes and fighting around the police station in Glina?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several documents cited in this report that clearly state that there were some armoured -- armed struggle going on in this area on those dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Based on the documents that you inspected, could you establish who the Serb forces were fighting against in Glina in the police station and around it?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to answer this question, I should go through again all these documents. I don't remember whether they explicitly state whom they were fighting in this area, but bearing in mind that these documents, or at least one of them, refer to victims of being civilians. I think that civilians were present in these areas as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The reports that you inspected with regard to the fighting in Glina, did they say anything about the armed opposition which had in its possession various weapons and that they had trenches and that the fighting was going on all day long? Did you find that in the documents?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not explicitly, but because some of these documents are basically situational reports, it's clear that there were two sides on this fight.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: The other party against the Serbs, was it armed, and was it under the control of the then Croatian authorities?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is something I can suppose, but now you ask me to conclude something on the -- or interpret these documents, and I don't remember so explicitly the content of these documents. I should go -- I should see them once again in order to give a precise answer to this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us which document you need? We can put it on the screen and help you with your testimony in this regard.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically all documents I'm referring to in chapter 1 of this part 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In other words, after having inspected all of these documents, all you can remember is what the Serbs did.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: These documents are explicitly documents written by Serbs about their actions. So there's no so much information with the other part or partner in this fight was doing. These documents tell what different Serb forces in the area were doing in this particular time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: With regard to the operation around Glina, you have stated that according to Captain Dragan's plan, as you say, and the War Staff in Glina, 700 civilians participated in the operation together with 50 specials and 50 policemen. And then you continue to say on page 28, or in B/C/S it starts with footnote 126, you say that the commander of the Special Unit called Sundac, Nikola Sundac, and you continue to say that he was also the commander of the sabotage unit, and in the fourth paragraph you say that Nikola Sundac's detachment is being mentioned by two reports. And finally in the fifth paragraph of -- paragraph of that page you say this unit was connected to Milan Martic, which is corroborated by the report on the work of the Special Police Detachment in Dvor Na Uni. In other words, the Executive Board of the municipality of Dvor Na Uni sent a special group for training. My question is -- first of all, let me tell you the -- the quote was rather long, but this is the methodology that you used in your work. Based on the fact that somebody mentions a special unit and then continues to mention a sabotage unit, then a special sabotage unit, is this enough for you to say that these men belonged to Martic? That is my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd object to the question. It misstates the evidence. The report, at least the part that's been cited by counsel, doesn't say that these men belonged to Martic. It says they unit was linked to Milan Martic. Perhaps it's a translation issue, but just to be clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My learned friend is right. I have already provided the witness with this document which speaks about the connection between Milan Martic and this detachment, and that is the essence of my question, and I am just specifying things in order to avoid any confusion with this regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are causing confusion, Mr. Milovancevic, when you say "belonged" instead of saying "linked." So be specific and quote what's said. Don't misstate the evidence. Now, Mr. Kerkkanen, was it sufficient for you to conclude that these people are linked to Mr. Milan Martic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, on the basis of these documents, yes, I think that there's enough evidence in the content of these documents sufficiently to link Mr. Martic with these units. And, more specifically, the fact that Exhibit number 2100, the report on the work of the police special unit in Dvor Na Uni, includes in the report this unit, the mere fact that they are dealt with the police report tells about the fact that this group was perceived to be linked to the police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Could we see on the screen Prosecution document 2437, 2437.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: What we will now see on the monitor, Mr. Kerkkanen, is a decision from the Executive Council of Dvor municipality dated the 31st of May, 1991, entitled "Conclusion." Do you recognise this document, Mr. Kerkkanen?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps you can scroll a little bit more down. Yes. I -- I recognise this document. What is the footnote number, may I ask? Because I believe I'm referring to this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Right now I cannot tell you precisely. It's one of the documents I marked, but now I find it difficult to find the footnote number. It's not on the page we are on at present. But as in the last paragraph of this report, on page 28 you say that the Executive Council of the Municipal Assembly of Dvor municipality sent a certain number of volunteers for training. My question to you, regardless of the footnote number, is the following: Does this conclusion show that the Executive Council sent a certain number of volunteers from their own territory, that is the territory of Dvor municipality, to be trained for Special Purpose Units for the needs of Dvor municipality, and they sent them to the Ministry of National Defence in Knin? Is that what this document says?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Milovancevic, in fairness to the witness you must find the footnote so that he can correctly jog his memory. To say you can't find it and regardless of the footnote you're just going to put the question is not helpful. I think the witness must get what he's asking for.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I can be of assistance on this document. I don't believe this document is cited in the report. This is a document that I went through with Mr. Kerkkanen as a -- that group of extra documents after we talked about the report, and it was admitted as -- as Exhibit number 471 during that process. So to my knowledge it's not cited in the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which document is not cited in the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The document that's on the screen, which is 65 ter Exhibit 2437, which is also in evidence as Exhibit number 471.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you hear that now, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I realise now that this document is not to be found in any of the footnotes, but Mr. Kerkkanen did comment on it when responding to the Prosecutor's questions, which is why I put my question to him. By Your Honour's leave, I would like to proceed with this question. This document, which bears the number 2437 from the 65 ter list, is not one of the footnotes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There's nothing wrong in you continuing, Mr. Milovancevic, if only you can be on the same page with the witness and we can all be following what you are talking about. Now, this document belongs to a separate set of documents, not the ones that are in the report. If you can get to that with the witness, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Witness, I assume you see what the problem is. Can you tell us to what group of documents this document belongs? I'm referring to document 2437. And then could you answer my question, please?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Now I remember. These are additional documents that are not cited in the report but were tendered as evidence. And I saw -- I have read through. I'm familiar with this document. And basically what you said about the content, it's accurate except for the fact that it doesn't state that it was ministry of national -- of the national defence but states Ministry of Defence in Knin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: As for the Ministry of Defence, Mr. Kerkkanen, I read the text in B/C/S where it says the Ministry of National Defence of the SAO Krajina in Knin. That's what is stated in the text of the document in B/C/S. I don't know how it's been translated into English. However, this detail does not affect your answer. Another question about this document: In this document, is the MUP of the Krajina ever mentioned, or Milan Martic?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in this document, but we have to keep in mind officially on the 31st of May, 1991, Mr. Martic held the position of Minister of Defence. He was appointed to this first on the 29th of May, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: And one further question about this document. Is it evident from this document that it refers to training in Knin, sending people from the territory of Glina to be trained in Knin for the needs of Glina municipality? Excuse me. I made a slip. I was referring to Dvor municipality. The entire document refers to Dvor. So it was a slip on my part. Are men being sent for training for Special Purpose Units for the needs of a particular municipality, the municipality of Dvor?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what -- what the document states.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll now move on to talk about paragraph 2 entitled "Bacin, Cerovljani, Dubica," and it begins with footnote 146. In the first paragraph you say that in Bacin, on the 20th of October or thereabouts, Croatian civilians were killed, and you go on to say that the annual report of the public security station in Dvor Na Uni, referring to the period between the 23rd of June, 1991, and the 1st of January, 1992, confirms that police units subordinated to Martic were active in Kostajnica and Dubica in 1991. My question is the following: Did you find in the documents the information that Serb forces entered Dubica, Bacin, Cerovljani, and Kostajnica on the 16th or the 15th of September, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We have heard this from witnesses, but as you don't remember, my next question will be about the quotation you include from this report. You quote the part that states that from the very beginning, the entire personnel of the public security station took part in all actions. Mop-up operations in the territory from Dvor to Volinja have within carried out. On several occasions they provided help in actions in Kostajnica, Glina, Petrinja, Dubica and other places, and that professional and technical aid has been provided to Kostajnica and other organs where it was needed. In connection with this, I wish to ask you whether it's evident from this report that these were combat activities carried out by members of the police of the SAO Krajina from the public security station in Dvor Na Uni. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's clear they are talking about combat operations as they refer to mop-up operations. Not exactly necessarily in Dvor Na Uni but from Dvor Na Uni in the areas of other nearby municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kerkkanen. In the documents you reviewed, did you find the information, as you mentioned the Croatian civilians killed in those places, that apart from any military or combat action the civilians in these places were gathered together, taken to a fire station, and killed? Do you have this information?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have this information on the basis of these documents related to the police units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that these civilians were rounded up and taken to the fire station?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think this is what the indictment states.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You go on to say in your text: Special Unit commander in Kostajnica, Stevan Borojevic, sent a request to Krajina Ministry of Interior on the 23rd of September, 1991, requesting that official status be granted. And then you go on to say that in January, 1992, Martic confirmed that Borojevic was commander of the Special Purpose Units in Kostajnica. My question is the following: Do these two documents show that Borojevic was not under Martic's command until January 1992; that Martic officially appointed him commander of the unit on the 13th of January, 1992? That's footnote 148.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the -- what this document states, but as I see on the basis of Exhibit number 661, Borojevic request on the 30th of September, 1991, to Martic, it's more like asking Martic confirmation the Special Unit is -- is under Martic's command. And I'm referring specifically to the text in this request, which state -- quoting Borojevic, "This is the only unit in this area that has remained under your command." So this shows that this unit was already at that time under Martic's command, but for some reason Borojevic wanted to have a confirmation of perhaps official status of this unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Did you connect this explanation provided by Borojevic with the first quotation from Borojevic's letter on this page where he says he does not want to be subordinated to the JNA and the command of the TO with his unit? He and his local unit on the ground did not want to be under JNA command, and so they wanted to be attached to Martic. Is that the reason for his request to Martic?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on -- what I can only state on the basis of this document is that it quite explicitly states this unit was already under Martic's command, because he states that "it has remained under your command." Whatever the reasons for this is the other thing, I don't -- I think is not so relevant in this context.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, in this context, only your conclusion is relevant, and your only conclusion that this is evidence that this unit was under Martic's command, that's what your conclusion is. Did you ever find any documents showing that Martic established in unit?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Basically it's not my conclusion. It's the conclusion that can be seen and read on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on. Saborsko, Poljanak, and Lipovanic. That's point 3 in your report. You say the main attack against Croats in the village of Saborsko took place on the 12th of November, 1991 between 0900 and 1400 hours. Please point us to the document which states that the aim or the goal of the attack on Saborsko was to attack Croats?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I don't have this kind of document at my disposal, and there is no document like this referred to in this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Why, then, did you say something like this in your report, that this was an attack against Croats?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I understand the basis of other well corroborated information, that's the fact that took place in -- in Saborsko.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In connection with the action at Saborsko, did you see a document on the order to Tactical Group 2 of the JNA? And in this order, Tactical Group 2, under the command of Colonel Bulat, is based on an order from the command of the 5th Military District, and it relates to an attack on Saborsko. Have you seen such a military document?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I have seen it, but in order to refresh my memory I should see it again in order to be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: From the documents you reviewed, did you see the term of a company in Saborsko? I'm referring to a unit of the Croatian armed forces.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next point, 4, refers to Skabrnja and Nadin. You say that Skabrnja and Nadin were attacked on the 18th and 19th of November, 1991. On the basis of what document, did you establish that Skabrnja and Nadin were attacked, and how do you know who started the attack?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, this introductory part of this paragraph 4 in this chapter has been based on well established facts. For example, found in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware, Mr. Kerkkanen, that everything that is in the indictment has to be proved in these proceedings? So these are not established facts.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: My next question: Did you find the information that in Skabrnja and the seven nearby villages which covered a third of Zadar municipality there were 730 armed men belonging to Croatian units and that they were equipped with boots, helmets, belts, shoulder-straps, automatic weapons, and other weapons? Do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know all these details, and in this context I think I have to remind that I wasn't undertaking a crime base analysis. I was looking for documents related to these events that the -- are talking about the SAO Krajina or RSK MUP units and forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: You say, Mr. Kerkkanen, that you did not establish facts concerning the crime base, and yet in the part about Dubica, Cerovljani, Bacin, Skabrnja and Nadin, this part is entitled the MUP of the SAO Krajina and the crimes committed in 1991. Why did you put this title there if you did not deal with the crime base?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't say that I don't deal -- or I didn't deal with the crime base. I said I didn't undertake a crime base analysis. This is something different. I deal with the crime bases when they are somehow related to the SAO Krajina MUP units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In connection with the events in Skabrnja and Nadin, after this introductory sentence saying when the attack against the villages of Skabrnja and Nadin took place, you go on to talk about the structure of the Benkovac police, about the most important persons in the Benkovac police department. You go on to speak of Goran Opacic who was in the public police station and was then transferred to the army. And then you go on to quote the reports about Skabrnja which were drawn up by Lieutenant Simo Rosic, by Ristic of the JNA. And then in the part that has footnote 131, you say there is a report by Ristic on the killings in Skabrnja indicating that members of TO carried out killings. In the next paragraph -- have you found the paragraph, Mr. Kerkkanen?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that you were referring to footnote 163, not 131 as you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. 163. Thank you, Mr. Kerkkanen. You go on to speak of an Official Note from Lieutenant Commander Simo Rosic and Major Milivoj Ostojic saying that the perpetrators were members of the Benkovac Territorial Defence Staff Special Units or units that fought under their command. And in the next paragraph you mention a report by Simo Rosic dated the 11th of March, 1991, which gives additional information. According to this information, the group that committed murders was headed by their commander at the time, Zoran Tadic, and besides him murders were committed by certain Serbian volunteers. My question is the following: The title of this paragraph 2 is the police in Krajina, SAO Krajina MUP and crimes in 1991. On what basis do you link Mr. Martic with these crimes? They all mention that it was members of the TO or other volunteers who committed these crimes.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think these investigations carried out in investigating reports written by the JNA at the time are important evidence. And as one of the reports, footnote 163, Exhibit number 1958, refers to the fact that the chief of Benkovac public security station, Mr. Drazic, was present during the attack in Skabrnja. First of all, it shows that there was or there were police units subordinated to Mr. Martic present in those areas, and furthermore, I was interested in finding whether Mr. Martic initiated any similar investigation on those events as the JNA did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient time, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It is the most convenient time for our first break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Then we will break off and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, on page 34 of the B/C/S version and the title Bruska, December, 1991, we are still talking about footnote 166, because a while ago we spoke about Bruska and Skabrnja. Bruska is our next topic. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. In several paragraphs here you're saying that the JNA investigated the killings, and according to the information in the first paragraph, a person known as Ranko stated that in Bruska village there was fighting between Dusko Marinovic and Mile Pupovac whose nickname was Kljaja, and the source whose pseudonym is Ranko believes that Mile Pupovac might be one of the perpetrators having revenge as his motive. Further on in the following paragraph you're quoting the report by Major Branislav Ristic of 4 April 1992. On the basis of his contacts with source known as Kota who informed him that the perpetrators were Pupovac and Skoric whose first names are not mentioned but they hail from Medvedja village. The information that you quote here on the investigation conducted by the JNA, do they point to the motive of the killing in Gruska such as has been mentioned by the indictment? In Bruska.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I speak here about the document, about the JNA investigation on this particular event, and this document speculates that this dispute perhaps has something to do with the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Further on, you say that in two MUP reports in Bruska the killings in Bruska are mentioned there, and you quote the report of the police station in Benkovac. Do you remember whether this report of the Benkovac police station that you quote is a report covering a certain period of time rather than just one day?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that one of these MUP reports covers various events. It's like events for a week or so. But in order to be sure, I should see this document. I think it's Exhibit number 679.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can P679 be shown on the monitor, please? Mr. Kerkkanen, you're referring to footnote 67 -- 172. Have we provided you with the right document number? Is that a document that you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It will be footnote 172, not 67 -- 172 as mentioned on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is the document that I have in my mind. So it starts -- it's a report for the period between 10th of December, from the 10th of December, 1991, until the 24th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Based on this document that is in front of you on the monitor, can you see what happened each day? And also, is it obvious, looking at the document, that this document speaks about the events that took place on the 12th of December, the 13th of December, and so on and so forth, and that the killings, the mortar attacks, and the suffering of the civilian population are mentioned? In other words, this is just a review of certain events that took place over a period of certain number of days that this report refers to?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that under a certain date when all of the things happened in Bruska, which is the 21st of December, 1992, is the massacre in Bruska mentioned? Actually, a more severe, more serious term is used than the one that you used talking about Bruska. I'm asking you that because of the fact that in two SUP reports these killings are mentioned just in passing. Is this a fair comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object to the question. I think it's exceedingly unclear. I'm not sure what the question is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, you're asking if it's a fair comment. I'm not sure what is a fair comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. My colleague is saying that my question has been misinterpreted. In other words, the interpretation did not reflect my question. My question was: Is it correct and does the witness possess material from in document based on which he can claim that this killing is mentioned only in passing, which implies that the SAO Krajina police is not interested in the killings, whereas on the other hand this report is just an overview of the events. And this was the gist of my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm still not understanding you. Whether this was just mentioned in passing is a statement that's introduced by you. Now you want the witness to justify what you are putting to him instead of justifying what he says. Are we together on that one?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in order for you to understand me fully, I would like to say that this is what I asked the witness. Within the context of the document that is on the monitor in front of us, which is an over -- a report, a summary report, is it correct to say that in two MUP reports the killings in Bruska are mentioned only in passing? Is it his testimony that such interpretation of the events as we can see on the monitor is correct? And this is the gist of my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But which two MUP reports are you talking about? Shouldn't he comment on the document on the screen rather than on the two MUP reports which we don't have before us?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm just quoting the first sentence in this paragraph, and I'm trying to quote correctly. I am quoting the whole sentence, and I repeat it. And the question is whether this report that we have on the monitor deserves such a comment on the part of the witness. And the second report is footnote 173 that the witness mentions further on. But we are not interested in the second report. We are only interested in the first report, the first MUP report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, maybe you understand the question. Are you able to answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. First I have to correct. You mentioned earlier December 1992. We are talking about the 21st of December, 1991. Basically by its nature the first document, Exhibit number 679, is a summary of events from the 12th until 24th of December, 1991. And the second, Exhibit number 677, is -- gives a little bit more detailed information as it lists names of killed persons and some additional information as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We shall move on to another topic. In the third part, and the title is "Connection between the MUP of SAO Krajina, i.e., the Republic of Serbian Krajina." I apologise. "A connection between the SAO MUP and the joint criminal enterprise and the linkage between the two." With regard to this title, I would like to ask you as follows: Based on which did you establish that there was a joint criminal enterprise? Which documents did you use in order to establish that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to object. Where -- I don't think that -- I don't think the report purports to establish that there was a joint criminal enterprise, notwithstanding the title. I don't think the title purports to make that conclusion. And I don't think that anywhere in the text does it purport to establish that there was a joint criminal enterprise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I perceive the objection as an explanation by my learned friend, and I would be very happy if the witness provided us with his own explanation bearing in mind that this is his report. And if the witness repeats what my learned friend has just said, I will be only too happy and I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That is true, but be that as it may, Mr. Milovancevic, if indeed the report does not purport to say that there was a link between -- the linkage between the MUP and the joint criminal enterprise, then your question becomes misleading. Do phrase your question in the context of the content of the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, this is your title that you have given to the third part, the linkage between the SAO MUP and the joint criminal enterprise, and then your first subtitle is "MUP training in Golubic." "The MUP units in the Posavina corridor." That's your second subtitle. The linkage between the SAO Krajina MUP and the ARSK MUP and Slobodan Milosevic. "The linkage between the SAO Krajina MUP and the Serbia MUP." And the second subtitle is "Training." Another subtitle is "Supply of armaments and logistics. All of the subtitles that I have provided you with can -- do not contain the word "joint criminal enterprise," but they are all subtitles in the third part that talks about joint criminal enterprise. With regard to that, do all these titles suggest the existence of the joint criminal enterprise, and do these subtitles actually refer to the existence of a joint criminal enterprise? That is the gist of my question to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do refer for the existence of active cooperation between different agencies on different operations in different areas, whether they were police, military, or other agencies from the SAO Krajina, the RSK, from Republika Srpska, and Bosnia-Herzegovina, or from the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Based on your answer, can I say that you believe that there was a linkage between the two and that there was indeed a joint criminal enterprise? Is that why you gave the third part this title?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Documents I reviewed for this report and I'm referring to show that there was a linkage between different agencies I was referring to in my previous answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: And one more question in this regard. Did you ever see a plan document on the so-called joint criminal enterprise which provides us with time, participants, goals, means, or any such thing?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. With regard to subtitle 1, "MUP training in Golubic," you're quoting Captain Dragan saying, "Our main objective should be those who have completed training, return to their homes and form mini training grounds wherever possible, as well as warehouses which would produce new formations." With this regard, the question for you is as follows: Such a statement by Captain Dragan, i.e., a report, does it point to the fact that the units trained were MUP units, and is that something that can be concluded based on this quote?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to answer this question, I would like to see this document. I think it's Exhibit number 1952.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell us what footnote are you referring to, Mr. Kerkkanen, and which document are you referring to, under which footnote?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's footnote 176.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have the document before you, Mr. Kerkkanen? Please look at it and then answer my question if you can.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you scroll down, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If I could be of assistance. I think that the document that was being discussed before with the quotation of "our main objective should be that those who have completed training should return to their homes," I think that is actually a different document. It is 783, which is cited in the next footnote, 177.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- I think you are correct. You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have this other document on the screen, please, on the monitor, 783 from the 65 ter list? Can you scroll down and go to the second page of the document? A bit further. I would like to see the second page of the document, if possible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, speaking specifically about this paragraph I'm quoting in the report, it does not say anything about the MUP. But the fact that the same document, and Captain Dragan in this document speaks about Milan Martic, it makes it clear that Milan Martic is linked to this training and what was happening in this training ground at Golubici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 38 of the B/C/S version, which is the next page and starts with footnote 182, you are saying in the middle of that page, which is above the subtitle under 2, "The RSK units in the Posavina corridor," above that title, the second paragraph above that title, it appears that SAO Krajina MUP ran a training camp also in Bosnia in Gornji Podgradci in the autumn of 1991. This is what you're saying, and you're explaining this by saying two applicants applying for SAO Krajina police refer in their CVs to the training they received for the Krajina police in Gornji Podgradci between 1 August and 7 October 1991. With regards to this, my question is as follows: Are you aware and do you have a document proving who it was who organised the training centre in Gornji Podgradci?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only documents referring to this training centre and training there are these documents referred to in this report, Exhibit numbers 1977 and 1978.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kerkkanen. Does this mean that these are the documents referring to these two applicants applying for the police from Podgradci? Is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: If two men are applying for the Krajina police, isn't that evidence that they are not members of the Krajina police? They're only applying to become members, and they explained that they completed some training somewhere, but they are only applying to become policemen. Isn't that direct evidence that they're not actually members of the Krajina police?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it has nothing to do with the fact that they got training, as they state in their documents, by the Krajina police.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, that's not what those two witnesses said. They said they completed training for the Krajina police but not from the Krajina police?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to object. Maybe we could refer to the documents, because I don't think that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you refer us to the documents, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. It's document 1977, footnote 186.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's have it on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can you see the document, Mr. Kerkkanen?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't -- now I think I have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Now you have it before you. I wish to know whether based on this document one can establish whether this refers to the SAO Krajina from which Mr. Martic hails or the Bosnian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We know that at that time the SAO Krajina police was in existence. Whether in the late summer and early autumn of 1991 Bosnian Krajina police was in existence, I doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: And finally, with reference to Gornji Podgradci, you didn't answer my question whether the fact that two candidates were applying to join the Krajina police shows that they were not in fact members of the police. Does it show this or something else?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my -- in my understanding, they didn't need to be members of Krajina police while they -- they undertook training by the police. The first statement -- statement of -- referred to states Nikola Babic saying, "I completed Krajina police training in Gornji Podgradci."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: That's all the documents you have referring to the Krajina police in Gornji Podgradci? Is that it, these two applications?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These documents are the only ones I have about training in Gornji Podgradci. But furthermore, I have to say that later on when the RSK was formed and a police organisation was systematised, on the basis of different documents I have seen that those who were previously working in the Special Police Units or linked with those units in order to become police officers they had to reapply for those positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We have completed this topic. The next subparagraph is "RSK MUP units in the Posavina corridor, Bosnia and Herzegovina." Here you say that the territory known as the Posavina corridor in Northern Bosnia was strategically a crucial one, as it linked the Republic of Serbian Krajina and the Bosanska Krajina to other Serb areas and Serbia proper. And this territory formed the most important supply route between these regions and Serbia. You then go on to mention a number of documents referring to fighting for the corridor and its participants. My question is as follows: Reviewing these documents and studying the combat activities of the Krajina police and other units, did you obtain information that at that point in time regular Croatian units, the 108th Brod Brigade of the Croatian army, the 109th Djakovo Brigade, the 102nd Djakovo Brigade, the Zagreb Brigade of the Croatian army, and the Rijeka Brigade of the Croatian army were on the territory of the neighbouring state, Bosnia and Herzegovina? These were regular Croatian units. And that they cut off the corridor. Do you know this, Mr. Kerkkanen?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see any documents referring this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the course of these proceedings, Prosecution Exhibit 711, which is a TV report from Belgrade on the corridor, was shown to witnesses, but as you haven't seen that report, I wish to know whether you found any documents showing that the government of the SAO Krajina asked the United Nations to open the corridor so that the population, the economy, health care, and everything else would be helped because it was facing a total collapse because of the incursion of Croatian units. Did you find that information?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. I don't recall seeing this kind of document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions about the corridor.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Excuse me. I'm sorry. Just for purposes of the record, there was reference to -- in one of the earlier questions just now to Prosecution Exhibit 711. I assume that's 65 ter number 711. Just to be clear. Not Exhibit number 711.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we clear that up, Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I was referring to the 65 ter list of exhibits. I thought I said that, but I may be wrong. I wish to remove any misunderstanding.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. While I'm just talking, Mr. Milovancevic, I just want to find out how much longer are you going to be with your cross-examination. I thought some other day the last time you had indicated that you needed only one session to finish off your cross-examination for today.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am drawing close to the end of my cross-examination. I don't think I will need much more time. I will try to use the time as efficiently as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I put to you several titles indicating a connection between the MUP of the SAO Krajina and the MUP of the Republic of Serb Krajina and the linkage with Slobodan Milosevic, as you put it, in your title, the links with the MUP of Serbia. And you enumerated a number of documents on supplies for the TO units and the Krajina police coming from JNA units, especially in early 1992. Is this correct, Mr. Kerkkanen? Do you remember these details, to avoid going through them one by one?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There are several documents indicating supplies coming from the JNA and to -- to SAO Krajina RSK TO army or police units, not only in 1992 but throughout the period from 1991 until 1995, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: And in connection with this, I wish to ask whether you saw in the documents that in 1991 the SAO Krajina was Yugoslav territory and whether from the Vance Plan and the report submitted to the Security Council you saw that on the territory of the SAO Krajina, under conditions of implementing the Vance Plan, Croatian legislation did not apply. It was Yugoslav legislation which applied. Do you know of such a report to the Security Council?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that the Federal Secretariat for National Defence as a federal organ was the only organ authorised to equip and arm all units on the ground, including on the territory of the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to object to that question. It goes beyond the scope of the competence of the witness. And also, it's vague. "Authorised to equip," I'm not sure what that means. Under whose authority and what that means. But most importantly, it just goes -- it goes beyond the scope and competence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question, Your Honour, had to do with the reports quoted by the witness, documents mentioning the Federal Secretariat for National Defence as the highest organ issuing orders to rear bases and JNA units in connection with equipping and arming all the units on the ground. I wanted to be brief and expeditious, so I didn't mention the documents one by one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any reply?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, I just understood the question to be seeking some kind of legal conclusion in the way it was asked. "Authorised -- the only organ authorised to equip." If there is a document that states that if it was the only organ authorised to equip we can look at that and comment on it, but otherwise I think that counsel's asking the witness to draw a legal conclusion which is not appropriate for him to draw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, do you have a document or documents? I know you say because of time you don't want to mention them, but at least one that you can refer to which says that, and let the witness comment on that document or group of documents?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The witness, in his footnotes, mentioned reports by the military expert Theunens, who spoke in detail on many pages of the powers and authority of the Federal Secretariat and the General Staff of the armed forces of Yugoslavia. If the witness can answer, please let him answer, but I don't wish to draw the witness into legal points.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which footnote specifically are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would have to look. We can resolve the issue in the following manner, Your Honour: We can ask the witness whether he is familiar with Mr. Theunens' report and whether he reviewed that document as Prosecution -- a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, pursuant to the request of Defence counsel, the reference is to Mr. Theunens' report have been deleted because the trial -- under the Trial Chamber's order of 28 April 2006, because the Trial Chamber found that that lacked probative value. So those have been deleted. So much it's a little strange to be asking about that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Milovancevic, apparently Mr. Theunens' report has been deleted from this witness's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will withdraw my question, Your Honour, in this situation. You were asking me whether I could recall a particular footnote, and I wanted to say that this was in the expert report. I didn't want to leave the impression that I was saying something off the top of my head. But I will, however, withdraw my question. I will not insist on these explanations in order to save time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which expert report are you referring to? Is this witness an expert, testifying as an expert?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this was a slip on my part. I was referring to this witness's report, not an expert report. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: I wanted to touch on another topic, Mr. Kerkkanen. You will recall that we mentioned a report on the selection of personnel in the MUP, and in your appendix to your statement which is before you, you speak of training in many places, the training carried out by the Krajina police. You mention sending men to the school of the MUP in Zemun and in Banja Luka and so on. Do you remember these details?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can one draw a general conclusion that the training of police units of the SAO Krajina was carried out by means of public announcements calling on an unmentioned number of persons to apply for a competition? Is that so?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly. That was -- that was so in the RSK but not really in the SAO Krajina in 1991, and that's what I have seen on the basis of these documents I was using.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Could we see on the monitor 65 ter document 747. It's actually a series of three documents having to do with the application of a candidate who wanted to enroll in the secondary school of the Ministry of the Interior. The first of these documents is dated the 16th of June, 1993, and it's an application for enrollment in police secondary school. Do you see that document before you, Mr. Kerkkanen? In this document, the applicant - could we scroll up a little bit - whose first and last name are mentioned here, and his signature is on the original, is applying to enroll in the school. Could we look at the next page of the document, please -- or, rather, the next document belonging to this sequence. This is a report dated the 27th of August, 1993 by the Secretariat of the Interior in Knin, and it's information of enrollment in police secondly school. Is that correct, Mr. Kerkkanen? And on the list we see the candidates who were not accepted. The candidate under number 8 is the one who applied in the first document. Is that correct, Mr. Kerkkanen? That's Aleksandar Tisma, in fact.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Can we see the next document in this sequence? This is a document issued by the Secretariat of the Interior, Knin, Drnis public security station, and the date is the 30th of June, 1993. Is that correct, Mr. Kerkkanen? And in this document, the candidate, Aleksandar Tisma, is mentioned and the following is stated: "Aleksandar, resident in Drnis, has been -- has taken a rather disrespectful attitude. He socialises with his peers [realtime transcript read in error "pierce"] as well as with people older than him who are prone to stealing, harassment of older citizens of Croatian ethnicity, and he usually takes the initiative in this. He is rather arrogant and impertinent to the employees of the MUP ..." And this report is signed. Is that correct, Mr. Kerkkanen?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Are these three documents, in your view, evidence that when applying for the Ministry of the Interior the candidates were checked? Their personal characteristics and ethical standards were checked? And here a candidate who in wartime conditions is prone to maltreatment of ethnic Croats was rejected. Doesn't this document show what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, it shows, and it has been -- I mean, it's also -- what I can say, on the basis of other documents that increasingly and in the RSK this was the procedure, but this was not the procedure in the SAO Krajina in 1991. So there was a gradual development in the police forces. In the RSK it became more systematised and became more like a professional police force, but that took place later, not in 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I guess the word "pierce" at line 19, 39, 19 is supposed to be spelled p-e-e-r-s instead of p-i-e-r-c-e. I don't know whether we could correct that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are right, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milovancevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And in connection with your last reply, Mr. Kerkkanen, with regard to the situation in 1991, did you find any documents showing that in 1991 the police of the SAO Krajina was composed of those policemen who belonged to the Ministry of the Interior of Croatia and who were dismissed because they were Serbs and who subsequently arrived on the territory of the SAO Krajina having left their previous employment? Did you find this information?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember seeing any specific documents to this extent.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: My final questions to you are as follows: Can you tell us what was your task when you analysed this topic? What was the exact task given to you by the Prosecutor's office?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My task was to locate SAO Krajina and the RSK MUP documents, select relevant documents to this case and carry out analysis of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In response to my learned friend, you stated that you looked at over a hundred thousand pages of material, that you selected some 20.000 pages, and that these 20.000 pages comprised some 3.000 documents. Judging by the number of footnotes and lists of documents that you have provided us with, we're talking about some 270 or 300 documents at the most. Can you please tell us, based on what criterion did you select the documents that you did out of the 3.000 that you have ended up after your -- your initial search?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I have to state that in the beginning of my testimony I gave my estimation that I personally reviewed between 50 to 100.000 pages of documents, not over 100.000. And secondly, the criteria basically for selecting those documents for this report was exactly based on my task, SAO Krajina and RSK MUP documents related to this case and Mr. Martic as the Minister of Interior, documents which are relevant and which shed some light on those events mentioned in the indictment against Mr. Martic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Let me be very specific. Was your task, in your capacity as an employee of the Prosecution, to choose such documents that would prove Mr. Martic's guilt in this case?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: My task was look generally at all the SAO Krajina and RSK MUP documents, including exculpatory evidence or information concerning this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Were any such exculpatory documents included in your report?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my understanding, yes. For example, it can be said that those reports related to the Baklajic and Silt group and that the -- some disciplinary action was taken against him can be considered as exculpatory evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kerkkanen. This concludes my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milovancevic. Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: No re-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Mr. Kerkkanen, first I would like to clarify the date of a certain document contained in this additional spreadsheet we received about the documents we later learned about, and this is concerning this document number 12. We discussed this today. I didn't want to disturb your dialogue, but I just wanted to clarify. Our Exhibit 471, which is 65 ter number 2437, this decision to send volunteers for Special Purpose Unit training of the MOD SAO Krajina in Knin, signed by the president of the Executive Council Vajagic, and it says -- in the column "Date" it says 31st of March. Shouldn't it be 31st of May, as it says in the next column? This is just a clarification. It may be just a simple error.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I should see that document before giving an answer. I don't recall it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes. Can we see the document Exhibit 471, 65 ter 2437. Yes, here it is. It says -- in the English translation it says Dvor, 31st of May. And in the original version it says the same, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: It is May, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's May. I see only this one. I don't see the 31st of March. Is it in the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: No, it's only on the spreadsheet we received.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, then there must be an error in the spreadsheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Now, this is more a question to you as to your impressions when going through all these documents. I have two questions as to your overall impression. We had this dispute about the Latin or Cyrillic types. Do you remember? If written on typewriter, to which extent about -- to which extent were these documents typed in Latin and to which in Cyrillic?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, understandably I can't -- it's impossible to give exact figures, but certainly I can state that the vast majority of these documents, typed documents, were written in Latin script.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you. And are those documents which we saw mainly carbon copies, and would that -- if yes, would that explain the missing signatures?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And to your experience, this is because in certain archives there are carbon copies, whereas the originals must be somewhere else? Do I understand correctly?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, exactly. As usually was the case, documents were made in several copies, distributed to several recipients, and therefore it explains that in copies, not necessarily --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: And these are not photocopies. These are classical carbon copies, are they, in many cases?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: In many cases, yes. And we were able to find -- in several cases we were able to find duplicates of some documents basically which was showing that they were distributed according to the distribution list they had at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HOEPFEL
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Yes. At the end of your cross-examination on Friday, you were asked about weapons stored in the depots under the control of UNPROFOR, and it was rather in their presence. Now, you said later that you saw weapons stored in the fields or, rather, I think it was light artillery. What did you mean by this?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I didn't say they were stored in the fields.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Or in the fields, rather. My correction.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I saw light artillery pieces deployed in the field with information that they were ready for use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: When you say "in the field," what exactly do you mean? In one place, more than one place, where? And what sort of artillery was it, for my own understanding?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- I recall one place. I don't remember, or I don't know exactly what was the exact location. Perhaps something like 20 kilometres from Knin, but certainly in the RSK area. And by light artillery I mean something like 122 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: When you saw the light artillery, did it appear to be in the control of or in the presence of any particular persons or troop or formation?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, as far as I saw, there was only presence of the RSK military in this location, and certainly there were not UNPROFOR personnel around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Now, in respect of the Samarica training centre and the Special Purpose Units created by the Executive Council of Dvor Na Uni Municipal Assembly on the 18th of June and whether Mr. Martic participated or, rather, influenced the decision, you answered that based on documents on the 18th of June, 1991, officially, Minister Martic -- Mr. Martic was Minister of Defence and not Minister of Interior. Now, it was left open-ended. What is the effect or result of that distinction?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, in this case I think there's no effect. They and these units were linked to Mr. Martic irrespective of the fact whether he was Minister of Interior or Minister of Defence at that moment, and at that moment he was Minister of Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Now, you were asked questions about the Predrag Baklajic group. I hope I'm pronouncing it right. And an order given re: The disbanding of the group and investigations carried out in relation to the group. I want to know by whom were the investigations carried out, the nature, extent, and the result or consequences based on the document which you said were referred to in investigations.

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I refer to the exhibit number 753. This is Knin SUP Secretariat of Internal Affairs Crime Prevention Department Report that gives information about criminal activities of Baklajic and his group. And the order to disband this unit came also from -- came also from Milan Martic, and this information is provided by the report Exhibit number 688, also from Knin SUP Secretariat of the Internal Affairs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to refer to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Honourable Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm so sorry. I'd like to refer to the video clip, Exhibit 478, and there is a reference to a press conference in Belgrade, soon after which Mr. Martic was interviewed about internal conflict in the leadership of the Krajina, and it's a clip in respect of Natasa Kandic in Belgrade. Now, you then say the first part of the clip makes it clear that it took place soon after the peace conference in The Hague in October, November. What does that refer to? Or should it be press conference in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, it refers -- I mean, this clip is from the press conference in Belgrade, and the press conference took place soon after the peace conference in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: And what did that peace conference in The Hague refer to?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, for the purpose of this clip, it just helped to date this interview with Mr. Martic, that it took place in the autumn of 1991.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Now, you were asked about a letter written by a group of policemen who were ethnic Serbs from Knin police station to General Petar Gracanin in early 1990 expressing discontent in respect of the insignia that they were being requested to wear and complained in respect of charges. You said you knew of the letter, but you didn't remember the contents. Now, from what you are able to recollect, was Mr. Martic one of the policemen who were complaining?

utterances.speaker: ARI KERKKANEN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I expressed myself by stating that I'm aware of the existence of this document, but I didn't refer to this document, as far as I remember, in my report, and I don't recall whether names of those policemen were complaining included the name of Mr. Martic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
utterances.text: Thank you. I do have a few more questions, and I'm looking at the time having gotten an indication from the Presiding Judge. I apologise to everyone for overextending somewhat, but I am feeling a little under the weather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: There's nothing to apologise for, Judge. I just thought you have a few more questions. I thought we could round up for the day, but it does look like if you have more questions we may have to come back for the third session this afternoon. So we're going to have to take an adjournment and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NOSWORTHY
